defect.locator_note: content_page.md Treatment & subsequent history; lake treatment.edges and treatment.derivation
defect.problem: The good-law call itself stands, but content_page.md overstates the treatment history by saying there is no negative treatment of Acevedo while the lake record contains proposed negative/query-hit progeny edges and audit_needed flags. The disclosed record supports good law and no point override, not an unqualified no-negative-treatment statement.
defect.proposed_fix: Keep Status: good as of 2026-06-30 and Binding — SCOTUS, but replace the categorical no-negative-treatment sentence with: Lake marks Acevedo itself as good law; proposed negative progeny hits are audit-needed and only marked mentioned, with no point override recorded.

reasons: Lake treatment directly supports field_i_validity good_law, as_of_treatment 2026-06-30, varies_by_point false, and the scope note that Acevedo itself is good law.
Authority weight is supported by court_level scotus and court U.S. Supreme Court.

However, the full treatment record includes 29 proposed edges with field_ii values overruled, abrogated, or questioned; all are field_iii mentioned and point null, so they do not refute good_law but do undercut the absolute no-negative-treatment wording.
residual_risks: Because lane1_negative and lane2_top_cited are audit_needed, the disclosed files do not conclusively clear every proposed negative progeny hit.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Say Acevedo is marked good law as of 2026-06-30 and has no recorded point override, rather than saying there is no negative treatment.
